headline: Camera first: the quantify agent reads the rate from the plume the camera sees, then checks it with the sensor models the case allows.

site.surface_basis: Flat gravel pad in open desert; equipment is an open skid, no enclosure

methods.label: Camera quantification (QOGI)
methods.how: Reads the methane column in every plume pixel from the radiometric infrared frame (thermal contrast against the background), sums it into the plume mass and multiplies by the plume speed measured between frames. Needs no anemometer.
needs: Thermal contrast of at least 2 K
methods.best_when: A visible plume; with or without wind data

methods.label: Gaussian plume
methods.how: For each candidate location, a steady Gaussian plume predicts what every methane sensor should read per kg/h in the measured wind. A non-negative least-squares fit gives the rate and how well that location explains the readings.
needs: Steady wind (direction spread at most 30 degrees)
methods.best_when: Several sensors, a few candidate sources, steady wind

methods.label: Backward Lagrangian stochastic (bLs)
methods.how: Releases tens of thousands of virtual particles backward in time from the sensors through the measured turbulence (WindTrax-style). The time they spend over the source gives the concentration per kg/h.
needs: Sonic anemometer: friction velocity and stability (Obukhov length)
methods.best_when: One known source, sensors close by, stability measured (night or day)

methods.label: Gaussian puff
methods.how: Tracks a train of small puffs, released every quarter second and each carried by the wind of its own second, so the plume can bend as the wind turns.
methods.best_when: Wind direction changing during the window

methods.label: pyELQ (plume + Bayesian)
methods.how: Shell's open-source inversion: Gaussian plume physics with Bayesian sampling over where sources are and how big.
methods.best_when: Many sensors, several leaks at once, steady wind

methods.label: MDLQ (puff + Bayesian)
methods.how: Detects, locates and quantifies from a continuous network: Gaussian puffs with a spike-and-slab Bayesian model that gives each source a leak probability and a rate range.
needs: Ring of sensors around the site
methods.best_when: Many sensors, several leaks at once, changing wind

methods.label: CFD + inversion
methods.how: Solves the airflow around buildings and equipment, then inverts the readings through it.
methods.best_when: Enclosed or built-up areas where air flows around obstacles
